newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-TACTICS USED BY REAL MADRID AND ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TACTICS USED BY REAL MADRID AND ATLETICO.

text.p: A look at the strengths and weaknesses of Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid who meet in the Santiago Bernabeu stadium on Saturday (1830 gmt).
Real Madrid

Strategy: Fabio Capello uses a modified 4-4-2 formation, but has been widely criticised for negative tactics, excessive reliance on counterattacks, and for introducing a long-ball philosophy to a group of skilful players capable of producing much better. Neverthless he has achieved results.

In defence Christian Panucci will probably move flanks to the left, Fernando Hierro and Rafael Alkorta will hold the centre and a substitute, possibly 'Chendo' Porlan, will take Panucci's place on the right.
Fernando Redondo and Clarence Seedorf will provide the link with midfield, with Raul Gonzalez pushed further up on the left.
Capello may also bring back experienced former captain Manolo Sanchis in favour of Emilio Amavisca or Victor Sanchez to secure the centre.
The heavily left-sided Davor Suker tends to switch back and forth with strike partner Predrag Mijatovic up front.
Strengths:
Goalkeeper Illgner is a tower of strength at the back, while both his substitutes -- Canizares and Paco Buyo -- would stroll into practically any European club side.
Fernando Hierro is not only the mainstay of the defence but is also strong coming forward through the middle and at set pieces.
The Balkan strike pair of Suker and Mijatovic are also dead-ball experts and it is in their individual brilliance, together with that of teenager Raul Gonzalez, that Real's true strength lies.
Perhaps because of Capello's tactical mastery, Real are masters in the art of turning round games -- having come from behind to win a dozen times already this season.
Weaknesses:
Under Capello Real have played effectively but with little style, and still don't play well as a team. The side relies excessively on Mijatovic, Suker and Raul making the best out of half-chances.
The long-ball philosophy, which Capello denies, means that at times the midfield seems not to exist at all.
And there are problems at the back.
Despite signing Illgner because of Capello's insistence on buying a taller keeper, Real have been particularly vulnerable in the air.
But the main headache faced by the ex-AC Milan coach is posed by the absence on international duty of left full-back Roberto Carlos -- a player who was nearly ever-present throughout the season.
Carlos' extraordinary swirling free-kicks will be badly missed, as will be his speed and commitment in breaks down the wing.

In practice games earlier this season Capello tried midfielder Emilio Amavisca in Carlos' place. But Amavisca fared disastrously when asked to do the same by Spanish national coach Javier Clemente last week, and the experiment is unlikely to be repeated.
Instead Panucci is likely to switch flanks, leaving his place on the right to the veteran Chendo.
Capello has solid performers, but no real match-winners, to call upon from the bench and is woefully short of capable reserve strikers.
Motivation: Capello summed up the motivation of both players and supporters: "Winning the title against Atletico is the best thing that could happen to a Real fan."

Likely team: Goalkeeper-Bodo Illgner. Defenders-Christian Panucci, Fernando Hierro, Rafael Alkorta, 'Chendo' Porlan. Midfielders-Clarence Seedorf, Fernando Redondo, Manolo Sanchis, Raul Gonzalez. Strikers-Davor Suker, Predrag Mijatovic.
Atletico Madrid
Strategy: Atletico's Radomir Antic also uses a variation on a 4-4-2 formation.

In the absence of injured defender Delfi Geli, Antic is likely to use Carlos Aguilera to secure the right, with Santi Denia and Roberto Solozabal in the middle and the lightning-quick Toni Munoz on the left.

Radek Bejbl or Juan Vizcaino will be given the job of linking the defence with midfield, where Jose Luis Caminero will once again take on the playmaker's role. Hard-tackling Argentine international Diego Simeone and set-piece ace Milinko Pantic complete the picture in midfield, with Kiko Narvaez generally playing behind fellow striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider up front.
The back four tend to push well forward to decrease opponents' room for manouevre, while goalkeeper Jose Molina does a sweeper's job by cleaning up at the back.

Traditionally Atletico have been a counterattacking unit, happy to sit back and wait for their opponents to attack while Barcelona and Real Madrid have been ball-playing sides that try to control the game.
Radomir Antic's Atletico are no exception to this rule and while capable of putting together patient build-up moves, are undoubtedly at their best bursting out of defence.
Strengths: Charismatic coach Antic turned relegation candidates into a double-winning side last season. As a motivator, Antic is the single most important factor behind Atletico's success.
Molina is a powerful force at the back, and leads a solid defensive unit that was Spain's meanest last season.
In midfielder Caminero's vision and Kiko's cheeky improvisation, Atletico have two potential match-winners, while Pantic creates constant danger at set-pieces.
Weaknesses: Although Molina and most of the back four and Vizcaino are dependable characters, too many of Atletico's players suffer from weak temperaments.
Caminero, Simeone and Esnaider in particular are all known to lose their heads and get sent off. Pantic also has too many off days, and has lost his form in dead-ball situations this season.
Tactically, Molina's tendency to play well outside his goal leaves him vulnerable to long distance shots.

Atletico must wait to see if Argentine midfielder Simeone is ready to play after flying back from last weekend's World Cup game. Without him, Atletico may be short of energy in the battle with Seedorf and Redondo.
Caminero is likely to start the game, but has been dogged by injury and has not hit his best form this season.

But Atletico's main weakness, and the principal factor behind their elimination from both European and Spanish Cups this season, has been a lack of firepower up front. Esnaider has missed a hatful of chances and several penalties and his days at the Vicente Calderon seem to be numbered.
Additionally Atletico lack the strength in depth of Real, who usually leave a couple of internationals on the bench and several more in the stands.

Motivation: Defeat, or even a draw, would leave Atletico as unwilling onlookers to the celebrations of 106,000 Real fans. Antic's side are still smarting from January's 4-1 drubbing by Gonzalez and company, and the Atletico camp is tired of being ignored by the press while Real and Barcelona get exhaustive media coverage.

Likely line-up: Goalkeeper-Jose Molina. Defenders-Toni Munoz, Roberto Solozabal, Santi Denia, Carlos Aguilera. Midfielders-Milinko Pantic, Jose Luis Caminero, Juan Vizcaino, Diego Simeone. Strikers-Kiko Narvaez, Juan Eduardo Esnaider.
